failed_deploy.description:
The newest deploy that failed after `deploy`, or `null`. A failed
deploy leaves the previous record current, so `deploy` and
`packages` describe that record.

leaving.description:
Objects of this cluster that left its build and are still being
deleted, because a finalizer or a slow shutdown holds them.

lock.description:
The run that holds the cluster's deploy lock, or `null` when none
does or this account may not read the lock. `kix status` never waits
for the lock and never takes it.

notes.description:
Warnings about the cluster, such as a platform interface that
changed.

objects_from.description: Where Kix found the list of objects the deploy made.

deployed_with.description: The version of Kix that made the deploy, when the record says.

Drift.description: The drift check of one object.

foreign_owners.description: Other field managers that own fields of the object.

unrecorded_scale.description:
A replica count changed through `/scale` that Kubernetes recorded no
owner for.

oneOf.description:
Kix has no applied hash for the object. A `kix deploy` of a Kix
cluster read from revisions applies it again and records one.
The object has no field ownership entry for Kix.

FailedDeployStatus.description: A deploy that failed after the current one.

failed_at.description: When it failed (RFC 3339), when the record says.

packages.description:
The objects of the failed build that the current deploy does not
have, by package, with the same checks as the cluster's `packages`.
They do not count in the cluster's `summary`, which counts the failed
deploy itself under `failed_deploys`.

reason.description: Why it failed, when the record says.

server.description: The URL of the context's API server in the kubeconfig, when known.

uid.description:
The UID of the `kube-system` Namespace, which `cluster.kubernetes.uid`
names. `null` when this account may not read it.

version.description: The version the API server reports, such as `v1.33.1`.

LeavingStatus.description: An object that left the build and is still being deleted.

finalizers.description: The finalizers that still hold it.

group.description: The kind's API group. Left out for the core group.

package.description: `namespace/instance` of the package it belonged to, or `null`.

LockView.description:
What a command that only reads says about a lock: who holds it and how
long ago it was renewed by this machine's clock.

activation.description: The record the holder is deploying, if any.

probably_dead.description:
Whether that is longer than the lease, so the run has probably died
and the next run that changes the cluster takes over. Clocks of two
machines can disagree, so this is a guess, not a decision.

renewed.description: When the holder last renewed the lock, by its clock, in RFC 3339.

seconds_since_renewal.description:
Seconds from `renewed` to now by this machine's clock. Negative when
the two clocks disagree, and `null` when `renewed` does not parse.

ObjectsFrom.description: Where Kix found the list of objects a deploy made.

oneOf.description:
The depends-on annotations of the deploy's live objects, for a record
written before Kix stored an index.

Nowhere: the record has no index and its own object is gone. No
object was checked.

time.description: When the manager last wrote (RFC 3339), when Kubernetes recorded it.

unshared_paths.description:
The paths in `paths` that Kix does not also own. Only these can stop
a deploy on a field ownership conflict. A field Kix also owns still
holds the value Kix applied.

PackageStatus.description: One package, or the cluster-level objects.

name.description: `namespace/instance`, or `null` for the objects no package owns.

Present.description: Whether an object is on the cluster.

oneOf.description: An import marker, which stands for an object Kix does not manage.
This account may not list the object's kind.

The object's record does not say its API group, and more than one
group on the cluster serves its kind, so Kix cannot look it up.

Problem.description: Something a check found wrong with an object.

oneOf.description:
The object is not on the cluster. Every check reports it, because
none can run on an object that is gone.
The object no longer holds what Kix applied.

The object is being deleted, so it will soon be missing. Every check
reports it, in place of `changed` or `not_ready`. The next deploy
waits until it is gone, then creates it again.

Purpose.description: Why a run holds the lock.

oneOf.description:
The operator corrects drift from the current record. It gives the
lock to a run that waits for it, and does not count as a write.
The operator deletes the objects of a deleted record.
A purpose a newer Kix wrote.

deleting_since.description:
When the object's delete started (RFC 3339), when it is being
deleted.

drift.description:
The drift check, or `null` when it did not run or the object is not
on the cluster.

finalizers.description: The finalizers that hold an object being deleted.

group.description: The kind's API group. Left out for the core group.

hash.description:
The hash the deploy record gives the object. For a deploy by this
version of Kix it is a hash of the manifest Kix sends for it. For a
deploy by an older Kix it is the object's identity hash annotation.

kind.description: The kind, or `Unknown` when Kix cannot name a missing object.

named.description:
`false` when Kix could not name a missing object. The deploy record
names its objects from Kix 0.10, and Kix's local store names them
when it holds the build.

needed_by.description:
The objects that depend on this one, as `Kind.group namespace/name`
(`Kind namespace/name` for the core group), when it is missing.

not_checked.description: Whether a selected check could not run on the object.

not_ready_reason.description: Why the object is not ready, such as `0/1 ready, 0/1 updated`.

problems.description: What the checks found wrong. Empty when the object is fine.

ready.description:
Whether the object is ready. `null` when the readiness check did not
run, the kind has no readiness (such as a ConfigMap), or the object is
not on the cluster.

oneOf.description: Is every object of the current deploy on the cluster?
Does each object still hold what Kix applied?
Is each object ready, by the rules a deploy waits on?

StatusDocument.description:
What `kix status` found. Programs that read it must skip fields they do
not know.

unreadable.description:
Resource types this account may not list, such as `secrets`. Objects
of these kinds that Kix cannot see are not checked.

Summary.description: Counts of objects. An object with two problems counts under both.

deleting.description: Objects of the build being deleted.

failed_deploys.description: Kix clusters whose newest deploy failed after their current one.

leaving.description:
Objects that left the build and are still being deleted. They are
not counted in `resources`.

ok.description:
Objects that every selected check passed. An object that a check
could not run on counts under `not_checked` instead.

description:
What `kix status` prints: the document, and how much of it the text
form shows.
title: StatusResponse
